ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, port A is located to the true east of observation point O, with OA = 4km. A ship sets sail from port A and arrives at point B after traveling in a direction of 15° north of east for a certain distance. At this moment, it is measured from observation point O that the ship is in a direction of 60° north of east. The question is, what is the distance the ship has traveled (i.e., the length of AB)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} Construct $AD \perp OB$ through point A, so that $AD= \frac{1}{2}OA=2\,\text{km}$. According to the problem statement, $\triangle ABD$ is an isosceles right triangle, hence $AB=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{km}$. Therefore, the distance traveled by the ship (i.e., the length of $AB$) is $AB=\boxed{2\sqrt{2}}\,\text{km}$.
